label: H.R. 7437

summary: H.R. 7437, titled the "Bridges And Safety Infrastructure for Community Success Act" or the "BASICS Act," amends federal transportation programs under title 23 of the United States Code. It establishes new funding set-asides and formula programs for strengthening bridges and regional transportation planning, modifies how funds are apportioned among states, adjusts local consultation requirements, creates a direct recipient status for metropolitan planning organizations, and covers 100 percent of the federal share for specific metropolitan and regional planning activities and off-system bridge projects owned by local governments or tribes.

affected_groups.effect: Must alter funding formulas, implement local consultation and suballocation mandates, run competitive processes before transferring safety funds, and adjust bridge and planning program allocations.

May qualify to become direct recipients of federal funding, receive direct sub-allocation of obligation authority, gain access to federal financial management systems, and expand the permitted uses of planning funds.
Receive dedicated formula and grant funding starting at a minimum of $300,000 per designated organization to support rural transportation planning, technical assistance, and capacity building.
affected_groups.group: Regional Transportation Planning Organizations and Rural Entities

affected_groups.effect: Benefit from required state consultation on local projects, potential 100 percent federal cost shares for local off-system bridge projects, and competitive funding access.

key_provisions: Establishes a strengthening bridges formula program providing $5.5 billion for each fiscal year between 2027 and 2031, distributed based on the relative cost of replacing or rehabilitating poor-condition bridges in each state.
Sets aside $150 million for each fiscal year between 2027 and 2031 to fund regional transportation planning organizations and rural economic development planning in nonmetropolitan areas.

Requires states to suballocate 25 percent of certain bridge and safety improvement funds based on population shares across various urban and rural area sizes, and mandates local project selection processes.
Sets the federal share to 100 percent for local, off-system bridges owned by local governments or Tribes, as well as for metropolitan planning activities.
Directs the Secretary of Transportation to establish a process allowing metropolitan planning organizations to qualify as direct recipients of federal funding and financial management systems access.
Imposes restrictions on states transferring safety funding by requiring a competitive process open to local governments and regional planning organizations first.
missing_information: The broader economic impact, total net cost beyond the specified set-asides, and exact changes to overall federal spending levels are not detailed outside of the specific program set-aside amounts.
Long-term effects on state highway trust fund revenues or non-transportation federal programs are omitted.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 7437, titled the "Bridges And Safety Infrastructure for Community Success Act" or the "BASICS Act," amends federal transportation programs under title 23 of the United States Code. It establishes new funding set-asides and formula programs for strengthening bridges and regional transportation planning, modifies how funds are apportioned among states, adjusts local consultation requirements, creates a direct recipient status for metropolitan planning organizations, and covers 100 percent of the federal share for specific metropolitan and regional planning activities and off-system bridge projects owned by local governments or tribes.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters federal transportation funding formulas and planning mandates to direct more resources and decision-making authority toward local governments, metropolitan planning organizations, and rural regional entities. It sets specific multi-billion-dollar funding levels for bridge repair and regional planning from fiscal years 2027 through 2031.
